correctness.rationale: The gradient test holds including p=3. The three sign involution quotients have the stated invariant function fields and smooth quartic genus-one models. For dx/y^3, x dx/y^3 and dx/y^2 the three nontrivial sign characters are distinct. Norm–pullback is [2] on each matching factor and zero across different characters (the mixed homomorphism equals its negative, so its connected image in 2-torsion is zero). Thus the product isogeny has 2-primary kernel and the geometric p-divisible groups agree. Compute the binary-quartic j-invariants over characteristic zero, then reduce the smooth models; this avoids the literal quartic-invariant fraction at p=3. CM by discriminants −4, −8, −4 gives inert classes {3,7}, {5,7}, {3,7} modulo 8, respectively. Add the elliptic contributions to get all four pairs and the ordinary, supersingular and superspecial assertions. Independently computed each elliptic Hasse invariant as the coefficient of x^(p−1) in the corresponding quartic to power (p−1)/2, via modular convolution for the first 24 odd primes through 97. At 3,5,7 the triples were (0,2,0), (4,0,3), (0,0,0); all 24 agreed. This does not replace the uniform proof.
residual_risks: The finite check tests the summands, not prime-to-p isogeny or the full Ekedahl–Oort type; those are not computational claims.

evidence: With d=4 and q=p, maximality is exactly p≡7 mod 8. Over F_{p²} maximality implies scalar Frobenius −p and hence superspecial reduction: on the Dieudonné module F²=−p and FV=p imply F=−V and a=g.

value.rationale: The genus-three degree-four Chebyshev curve is a natural named object from an established maximality problem. The mixed classes give precise, useful reduction data not available from the maximal-prime criterion and demonstrate the role of the distinct CM fields in one curve; this is a complete all-odd-prime exact invariant, not an isolated experimental observation.
residual_risks: The result is a narrow profile, not a classification of higher Chebyshev curves, polarizations or full Ekedahl–Oort types.
